claim: The surface breathes in a slow current — content drifting along a gentle flow field and back, like a reflection on calm water. Subtle, premium, content preserved.

q1_defects.answer: No blocking defects. The real card subject is fully preserved in every frame (dark navy body, amber/gold header bar, blue accent dot top-right, three grey content rows) — this is NOT a featureless tan/blue placeholder slab, so the #1 defect class that killed sibling tiles is cleared. Card content is tack-sharp at native resolution; no clipping, no broken frame. All four controls register changed=true. The only weakness is that the default idle/play animation is extremely subtle (near-frozen stills), not a defect per se but a discoverability note.

q2_reads_as.answer: Yes — reads as the claim at premium quality. control-duration-low warps the entire card into a curved trapezoid with bowing, tilted rows, exactly like a reflection rippling on calm water drifting along a flow field. control-breathing-high shows the card swelling/breathing with the accent dot displaced. The distortion is applied to the subject's own texture (header, rows, dot all carried into the warp), which is the load-bearing W3 invariant. Distinctly a flow/drift displacement, not a generic wobble.

q3_discoverable.answer: Partially. The idle.png is a clean, fully legible card that invites engagement, and the effect is unmistakably premium when parameters move. But at the default setting captured in play-1/2/3 the motion is barely perceptible in a still frame (frameDeltaMag drops 0.33->0.26->0.16 and frames are near-identical to idle). A first-time user glancing at the default tile may not notice the drift. The claim does specify 'subtle,' so this is intended, but it sits at the very edge of discoverability.

q4_responsive.answer: Yes — controls visibly change the look. duration-low shows a strong trapezoid water-warp vs the near-flat duration-high (cosine sweep lands different animation phases; metrics meanAbsDiff=1.944, changedFrac=0.0504). breathing-low is a calm card with the accent dot present, while breathing-high warps the card and displaces/shrinks the dot (meanAbsDiff=1.43). flowScale and drift differ more subtly between low and high. All four flagged changed=true.
evidence: metrics: duration meanAbsDiff=1.944 changedFrac=0.0504; breathing meanAbsDiff=1.43 changedFrac=0.0385

q5_net.answer: PLEASED. The effect is a genuine, content-preserving liquid/flow displacement of the real card, sharp and premium, with all four controls live. It clears the placeholder-slab defect class and reads convincingly as a reflection drifting on calm water. The only reservation is that the default idle motion is so subtle it nearly disappears in a still — a taste/discoverability flag, not a blocking defect, and consistent with the explicitly 'subtle' claim.

flags.note: The default idle/play animation is extremely subtle — play-1/2/3 are near-identical to idle (frameDeltaMag 0.33->0.26->0.16). The premium water-warp is only obvious when controls are pushed (e.g. duration-low). A first-time user on the default tile may not notice any motion. Consistent with the explicitly 'subtle' claim, but consider nudging the default drift/breathing slightly higher so the effect is self-evidently alive on first glance.
flags.evidence: flow-warp-idle/after/play-2.png vs flow-warp-idle/after/idle.png (near-identical); metrics: frameDeltaMag play-3=0.16

flags.note: breathing-high displaces/shrinks the blue accent dot noticeably while the card warps; verify this is intended flow behavior and not the dot being clipped at the displacement boundary.
